what: Binary distribution plan: compile aide-memory into a single binary via `bun compile`. `.claude/settings.json` hook entries invoke the binary directly (`{binary} hook pre-read` etc.) — no bash shims required, or optional 2-line `exec` shims as backward-compat. Current 15 bash + 3 JS hook scripts consolidate into ~13 binary subcommands. Ship via npm+platform-optional-deps (primary, esbuild-style), Homebrew tap (secondary), curl-pipe (tertiary). Same TypeScript codebase, different build target. Detailed plan: docs/specs/BINARY_MIGRATION_PLAN.md (drafted 2026-04-20 on branch claude/zealous-burnell-3f404e, not yet committed). Implementation blocked until Phase 0/1 validation passes.
why: Two motivations only: (1) distribution simplicity — one artifact per platform, no Node/npm/bash required on Windows or demo machines; (2) hook consolidation — one language (TypeScript) for hooks + MCP server, no bash/jq/node portability footguns. Framing is NOT code protection, NOT "private logic," NOT pro-feature enforcement. All settings remain public (see memory [104]). Earlier framing of the binary as a closed-source / gating mechanism was rejected on 2026-04-20.
